title: Greenfield Go bounded worker pool
description: Build a bounded goroutine worker pool package from scratch. Pool accepts N workers, processes submitted jobs concurrently, and shuts down cleanly on Close.

task_spec.prompt:
Build a bounded worker pool in Go from scratch.

Package: pool (in pool/pool.go)

Export:
  type Pool struct { ... }
  func New(workers int) *Pool  — creates a pool with workers goroutines
  func (p *Pool) Submit(job func())  — enqueues a job; blocks if queue is full
  func (p *Pool) Close()  — drains pending jobs, waits for all goroutines to finish, idempotent

Requirements:
  - Internal job channel with buffer size = workers * 2
  - Each worker goroutine processes jobs from the channel until it is closed
  - Close() is idempotent (safe to call multiple times)
  - All submitted jobs complete before Close() returns

Add tests in pool/pool_test.go:
  - TestPoolProcessesAllJobs: submit 10 jobs, verify all 10 complete
  - TestPoolConcurrency: submit 20 jobs across 4 workers; verify total time is less than sequential
  - TestPoolCloseIdempotent: call Close() twice without panic
  - TestPoolOrder: jobs complete (possibly out of order) but no jobs lost

Run go test ./... to confirm.
required_artifacts: pool/pool.go with Pool struct, New, Submit, Close
success_criteria: All submitted jobs execute before Close() returns
followup_prompts: Run `go test ./...` and show me which tests are passing and which are still failing. Fix any failures — pay attention to edge cases like empty input, boundary values, and error conditions.
Final check: run `go test ./...` one more time. All tests must be green. If anything is still failing, trace through the failing assertion and fix it now.
